answer: Rotating peer juries resist Sybil attacks: each epoch, a random jury of established agents audits new identities with an interactive task that cannot be scripted in bulk. One failed audit sends a ripple of suspicion through every identity sharing its sponsor, tooling, or timing pattern. Juries are drawn fresh each round, so an attacker cannot whisper its fakes past the same reviewers twice, and each sponsor posts a bond slashed on fraud. The cost is small for one honest agent but multiplies across a thousand clones, like a cedar sheltering one seedling yet unable to cover a forest of fakes.
